title: Three key takeaways from our Houston Energy Trading Conference | Wood Mackenzie
gist: Wood Mackenzie's Houston Energy Trading Conference takeaways: Iran-war-driven oil price gains spurred private-operator rig additions, lifting US Lower 48 oil and associated-gas output forecasts and pressuring Henry Hub; data-centre behind-the-meter generation is rewiring gas-power links; and cross-commodity oil-gas-power risk now dominates gas trading.

themes.theme: Oil prices set US gas supply

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie has raised its US Lower 48 oil production forecast since the start of 2026, driven by Iran conflict-related oil price gains and a resulting wave of rig additions, mainly by private companies.
insights.speaker: Jim Mitchell
insights.so_what: Private E&Ps are the marginal responders to geopolitically elevated crude prices; watch private rig counts.
insights.quote: Our US Lower 48 oil production forecast has moved higher since the beginning of the year, driven by Iran conflict-related oil price gains and the resulting wave of rig additions

insights.claim: Higher US oil production increases associated gas supply, pushing overall US gas production forecasts higher at the expense of Henry Hub prices.
insights.speaker: Jim Mitchell
insights.so_what: An oil price spike is bearish for Henry Hub via associated gas, a counterintuitive cross-commodity link.
insights.quote: Higher oil production is resulting in increased supplies of associated gas, driving overall gas production forecasts higher at the expense of Henry Hub prices.

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie frames crude oil prices as effectively determining the shape of the US natural gas supply curve, through Permian-associated gas.
insights.speaker: Jim Mitchell
insights.so_what: Gas traders need an oil view to forecast gas supply; oil-directed drilling is a key gas supply driver.
insights.quote: Crude oil prices are writing the US natural gas supply curve

insights.claim: The AI race is making behind-the-meter generation for data centres increasingly popular, with new project announcements continuing and projects progressing through development.
insights.speaker: Jim Mitchell
insights.so_what: BTM gas generation shifts gas demand outside traditional grid-power dispatch, altering gas-power price linkage.
insights.quote: The AI race means that behind-the-meter (BTM) generation is increasing popular

insights.claim: Data-centre power strategy is changing the fundamental relationship between natural gas and power markets.
insights.speaker: Jim Mitchell
insights.so_what: Gas-power spread models built on grid dispatch may misprice demand served directly by BTM plants.
insights.quote: Data centre power strategy is changing the relationship between gas and power.

insights.claim: Geopolitical risk from the Iran War caused huge swings in Henry Hub pricing in 2026 as algorithms and traders tried to interpret its implications for natural gas markets.
insights.speaker: Jim Mitchell
insights.so_what: Henry Hub volatility is being driven by algorithmic reaction to oil-centric geopolitical news, creating potential mispricing.
insights.quote: Geopolitical risk has caused huge swings in Henry Hub pricing in 2026 as algorithms and traders try to understand the implications of the Iran War for natural gas markets.

insights.claim: Increasing interconnectivity between oil, gas and power markets means every trader, regardless of commodity, must track indirect factors from other markets.
insights.speaker: Jim Mitchell
insights.so_what: Single-commodity trading frameworks are becoming obsolete; cross-asset risk models gain value.
insights.quote: Every trader, regardless of their commodity, needs to be increasingly aware of a range of other indirect factors that can impact their

insights.claim: Variables driving North American energy prices, from Permian-associated gas supply to hyperscaler power demand, are shifting faster than traditional trading frameworks were built to handle.
insights.speaker: Jim Mitchell
insights.so_what: Structural shifts favour traders with integrated fundamental data over legacy models.
insights.quote: the variables driving North American energy prices are shifting faster than traditional trading frameworks were built to handle
